title: God is saying to you today…
paragraphs: God is saying to you today…
“I have not forgotten you.”
And you almost didn’t believe it anymore.
Be honest.

There were nights you prayed… and nothing moved.
Days you hoped… and nothing changed.
Moments you smiled in public… but silently broke inside.
You started asking questions you were afraid to say out loud:

“Lord… did You skip me?”
“Did I miss my chance?”
“Am I still seen?”
And the silence felt louder than any answer.
But listen carefully—this is where many people misread God.

Silence is not absence.
Delay is not rejection.

Because if God had forgotten you…
Jesus would not have gone to the cross for you.
Let that sink in.

The cross is not a vague symbol.
It is a violent, bloody, undeniable declaration:
You are remembered.

Before you cleaned yourself up…
Before you got your life together…
Before you fixed your hidden sins…
Christ already chose you.
Scripture says:
“But God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” (Romans 5:8)

Not when you were worthy.
Not when you were strong.
Not when you were consistent.
While you were still broken.

So if He did not forget you at your worst…
Why would He forget you now?
But here’s the tension—you’re still waiting.

Still praying.
Still hoping.
Still wondering when things will finally turn.
And this is where the story gets real.
Because God’s “remembering” does not always look like immediate rescue.

Ask Noah—God remembered him, but the flood didn’t stop overnight. (Genesis 8:1)
Ask Hannah—God remembered her, but years passed before Samuel was born. (1 Samuel 1:19)
Ask Joseph—God was with him, but he still sat in prison before the palace. (Genesis 39–41)
God remembers… but He also prepares.
And preparation often feels like pressure.

It feels like being stretched when you’re already tired.
It feels like being hidden when you want to be seen.
It feels like being delayed when you’re ready now.

But God is not building a moment for you—
He is building a person within you.

A heart that can carry the blessing.
A faith that won’t collapse under pressure.
A life that reflects Christ, not just convenience.
And yes… sometimes that process hurts.
But don’t confuse the fire with abandonment.

Because the same God who allows the fire…
stands with you in it.

Just like He did with Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego (Daniel 3).
Just like He did through every generation of His people.

And most of all—
just like He did at the cross.
Because the cross looked like abandonment.
Jesus cried out:
“My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?” (Matthew 27:46)

For a moment, it looked like silence won.
Like heaven turned its back.
Like the story ended in loss.
But that was not the end.

Three days later—
the silence broke.
The stone rolled.
The grave lost.
And resurrection declared:
God never forgot.

So if you are in a “Saturday” season right now—
caught between promise and fulfillment,
between prayer and answer,
between pain and breakthrough—
Hear this clearly:
Sunday is coming.

Not because you earned it.
Not because you figured everything out.
But because Jesus already secured your hope.

You are not unseen.
You are not overlooked.
You are not abandoned.
You are held.
Even now.
Even here.
Even in the middle of your questions.

So breathe again.
Trust again.
Pray again.
And if you’ve drifted… if sin has pulled you away… if shame is whispering that you’re too far gone—
Come back.

Because the same Jesus who died for you
is still calling you.

Not with condemnation…
but with open arms.
Repent. Return. Receive grace.
He has not forgotten you.
He never will.
“The Lord is near to the brokenhearted and saves the crushed in spirit.” (Psalm 34:18)

Someone in your life is silently breaking right now—
and this might be the reminder they’ve been praying for.
God remembers.
